# A merge that kills a user and removes a secret must leave no orphans: the killed
# user's signkey and the removed secret's object are gone after finalize, while an
# unrelated user added on our side survives.

sesam-repo

exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec sh -c 'printf "secret\n" > gone.txt'
exec sesam add gone.txt --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob and a secret'
exists .sesam/signkeys/bob.age
exists .sesam/objects/gone.txt.sesam

# OURS adds carol (log divergence); THEIRS kills bob and removes the secret.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam tell --user carol --recipient $CAROL_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: add carol'

exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam kill --user bob
exec sesam rm gone.txt
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: kill bob, rm secret'

exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
exec git commit --no-edit

exec sesam verify
! exists .sesam/signkeys/bob.age
! exists .sesam/objects/gone.txt.sesam
exists .sesam/signkeys/carol.age
